value.rationale: The octahedron and cube are canonical Platonic dual graphs. This identifies an intrinsic G-equivariant homotopy and complete integral first-homology lattice for the natural perfect-matching complex, and explains exactly six missing extendibility obstructions through a signed integral quotient. The quotient character materially distinguishes ordinary and perfect matching topology, which is a motivated structural question in cited perfect-matching-complex research. This is not just recomputation of an ordinary Betti rank; limitations to the single canonical graph are explicitly stated.
